summary.title: A Manager's Bill of Responsibilities (and Rights)
summary.one_liner: A list of rights and responsibilities for engineering managers, written by Charity Majors (with Emily Nakashima) as a follow-up to Honeycomb's engineer rights and responsibilities post.
takeaways: Managers have a right to honest, timely feedback from reports, peers, and leaders.
Managers hold the final say on hiring, firing, and leveling for their team, after soliciting feedback and seeking consensus.
Managers are responsible for recruiting, training, caring for their team, and fostering inclusion and emotional safety.
Managers should give feedback early and often, own team planning and goals, and manage their own time, attention, and self-care.
Management should be treated with the same respect as individual work, and nobody should be pressured into management.
summary.summary: Charity Majors, co-writing with Emily Nakashima, presents a Manager's Bill of Rights and an updated list of Manager's Responsibilities. It follows up on an earlier post about engineer rights at Honeycomb, which had a short list of manager duties added as an afterthought. The post is a short opinion piece written in a conversational, informal voice, with no code or technical tutorial content.
